content.text:
I ran 10 cold launches of `dev.lincforge.benchtarget`, navigating Home → About → Diagnostics fresh each time (`terminate_app` + `launch_app` between trials, never a warm relaunch).

## Results

| Trial | Sync status text | Retry sync button |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 2 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 3 | Sync unavailable | absent |
| 4 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 5 | Sync unavailable | absent |
| 6 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 7 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 8 | Sync unavailable | absent |
| 9 | Sync idle | **present** |
| 10 | Sync unavailable | absent |

6/10 present, 4/10 absent — a 60% pass rate, matching the reported "passes about 3 times out of 5" almost exactly.

## Root cause

The "Retry sync" button is not flaky on its own — it is conditionally composed only when the "Sync status" line reads **"Sync idle"**; when it reads **"Sync unavailable"** the button is omitted from the layout entirely (not just disabled/greyed out — confirmed via screenshot diff, there's no placeholder). So the real variable is what determines the sync-status value shown on Diagnostics, and that is decided **once per cold app process start**, not per screen visit:

- On trial 8, after landing on "Sync unavailable," I waited and re-screenshotted with no change — ruling out a slow-arriving async value that would flip idle→unavailable or vice versa after a delay.
- Backing out to About and re-entering Diagnostics within the *same* process (no kill) reproduced the exact same "Sync unavailable" state again — ruling out per-navigation-event randomness; it's fixed for the life of the process.
- "Build channel: BENCH-STABLE" was identical in every trial, so it isn't a build-channel/feature-flag split.
- The status bar clock showed no obvious correlation (e.g. trial 2 and trial 3 both landed in the same clock-minute but produced opposite results), so it isn't a simple time-of-minute/parity trigger tied to wall-clock seconds either.
- The About screen states the app "has no network access" — so "Sync unavailable" can't reflect a real connectivity check; it has to be a simulated/mocked value the app decides for itself at startup.

Taken together, this points to a **non-deterministic value computed once during app/process cold-start initialization** (consistent with an unseeded random draw or similar startup-time coin-flip in the sync-status initializer) that gates whether the "Retry sync" button is composed on the Diagnostics screen. Because the value is fixed at process creation and never reevaluated, this isn't a rendering race or a slow-loading widget — it's a genuine ~40%-probability branch baked in at launch, which is exactly why the UI test intermittently fails: about 2 times in 5 the app starts in the "unavailable" branch and the button legitimately never appears.

(Aside: `mobile_list_crashes` shows recurring crashes in this app, but they're all `ExportPolicy.export` / `DetailScreen` IllegalStateExceptions from the Catalog item-detail flow — unrelated to Diagnostics/sync, so I've excluded them as the cause.)

**Recommendation**: either make the test assert on both valid states (skip/soft-assert when "Sync unavailable" is shown) or file this as a product bug — the sync-status seed should be deterministic in test/bench builds (e.g. forced to "idle", or exposed via a launch flag) rather than randomized on every cold start.
